recipes.name: Garlic Chicken, Vegetable and Rice Skillet
ingredients_raw: 1.25 pounds skinless, boneless chicken breast halves
1.75 cups Swanson® Chicken Broth or Swanson® Chicken Stock
1 (16 ounce) package frozen vegetable combination (broccoli, cauliflower, carrots)

steps.text: Spray a 12-inch skillet with the cooking spray and heat over medium-high heat for 1 minute. Add the chicken and garlic and cook for 10 minutes or until the chicken is well browned on both sides. Remove the chicken from the skillet.
Stir the broth, rice and vegetables in the skillet and heat to a boil. Reduce the heat to low. Cover and cook for 15 minutes. Stir in the cheese.
Return the chicken to the skillet. Sprinkle the chicken with the paprika. Cover and cook for 10 minutes or until the chicken is cooked through and the rice is tender.

raw_recipe.headline: Garlic Chicken, Vegetable and Rice Skillet
raw_recipe.description: You've got everything you need in just one-skillet . . . garlic-seasoned chicken breasts on a bed of rice mixed with colorful vegetables.  Getting dinner on the table couldn't be easier . . . and it tastes great too.

review.reviewBody: I made a few changes to this to suit our family. I was afraid that it was going to be a little on the flavorless side, but this surprised me by being a very good dish that my husband said was "stinking amazing". I used cous cous instead of rice, added about a clove more of garlic, and seasoned the chicken with seasoned salt and pepper. Followed the cooking directions to a T and it turned out amazing! I also used a blend of parmesan and asiago, and sprinkled some more on top when serving. Will be making this again!

Four stars, but only with my changes/enhancements. I used 4 breasts that were a good 1” thick totaling 1.5 lbs. I seasoned the breasts liberally with Adobo and Crazy Janes (my “go to” seasonings). The cooking spray was good to use to brown the breasts, but that’s about it. After browning I kept them in a warm oven. I added about 2 tbspns of butter to the pan and sautéed some left over chopped green onions and white onions that were in the fridge, and doubled the garlic (but I always at least double the garlic) until they were soft, not browned. Then added the rice along with ½ tspn rosemary, ½ tspn marjoram, ¼ tspn savory (mixed/crushed spices with a mortar & pestle). Let that cook for about 2 mins, then add the broth. I found that 1 ¾ cup was not enough and had to add some. I’d go w/2 cups next time. Heat to boiling, cover and reduce to low and cook for 10 mins. Then I added some frozen mixed veges and peas (not a fan of broccoli – vile weed – or cauliflower) and the parm cheese. After cooking for another 5 minutes I added back the chicken, covered and cooked for another ten minutes on low. The chicken was moist and the rice flavorful. I squeezed ¼ of a lemon over it all at the end. Next time I will only add the parm cheese and some lemon on the individual servings. The cheese, which I doubled, could not be tasted at all.

Good, but missing lots of seasoning! I sautéed a thinly sliced small sweet onion along with the garlic, and seasoned the chicken with salt, pepper, and paprika prior to cooking. I also added oregano, basil, and more paprika to the veggie/rice mix. A little dry, needed about 2 cups of broth rather than 1 3/4. Will make again! Served 2 for dinner with leftovers for lunches!
Good flavor but the frozen vegetables need to go in later.or be fresh.After they cooked so long they turned to mush. I also cut up the chicken to make it a one bowl meal.

A very easy weeknight dinner option. I substituted one sliced yellow squash in place of the frozen veggies and they were steamed perfectly by sitting on top of the rice while it cooked. Needed a little something to finish it off and a splash of lemon juice did the trick to add a lot more depth to the dish.

I was disappointed in this recipe. I seasoned the chicken with salt and pepper, which helped, but the rice was very bland and dry. It definitely needed some seasoning and a sauce of some kind. I won't be making this again. UPDATE: Rather than throwing out the leftovers, I cubed the chicken, added half a can of Progresso tomato cooking sauce, and stirred everything together. This made the dish much better.

Very simple (read: kinda bland), but I livened it up a little. Seasoned the chicken well & extra garlic after browning it. Also added frozen peas which I love. Some lemon juice and parsley at the end. I bet saffron would be good in this...

I made and it came out very good. I made some changes I cut the chicken breast into cubes, also made risotto rice made with broccoli and added Worcester sauce. My husband and I went back for seconds. Thank you for another great recipe.

The whole family really liked this recipe. I added a bag of frozen broccoli with cheese sauce (cheddar) and seasoned the chicken with salt, pepper and thyme. Also omitted the parmesan. May be a weeknight regular!

Pretty terrible. Absolutely flavourless and mushy.

This could be drastically improved if you substitute quinoa for rice, add the vegetables in at the end instead of the beginning, and use some spices for h*ck's sake!

As it stands, it's edible, but barely.

Yay an easy healthy dish and me and my husband both liked it! the only problem was that my garlic burnt:( 
still turned out though, because i just added some more after cooking chicken. Also used veg oil not spray, and cheddar cheese:) thanks!
Tasteless! Made as written, this is awful. I see where other reviews added so many extras in the way to seasoning. I wasted some good chicken breast on this.
No Changes - Good Flavor but not great. If you like garlic, add another clove. The veggies are very bland and you have to use salt and pepper to up the flavor.

I made this as a quick trying to be healthy meal. The chicken was bland, and the rice and vegetables were mush. I doubled the recipe but that is the only change I made. 
I will not be making this ever again!
Made it exactly according to directions and ended up with juicy mush and undercooked chicken
Won't make again, only eat half and I'm not fussy in the slightest. Very flavourless and the cooking times are wayyyy off. I'd make that many changes it would be a different recipe!
I made just a few changes so it will serve four people, overall a very delicious dish.

This is a good base recipe that can be modified & personalized in many ways. I'm only rating it a 3, because as written, it lacks in flavor. With the addition of different seasonings, the recipe can be suited to almost anyone's tastes.
Zero flavor despite doubling the garlic and Parmesan
Tasteless.
